analysis.summary: Analyzed the frozen axum 0.8.9 evidence and accounted for all 78 inventoried examples. Provided 13 complete src/main.rs recipes with explicit features and registry dependencies, separating current APIs from historical, compile-fail, ignored, and incomplete examples. Recipes have not been compiled or tested; validation remains with the coordinator. The sampled evidence is not exhaustive.

findings.title: Select server features and runtime dependencies explicitly
findings.guidance: Use Rust 1.80 or newer for axum 0.8.9. With default features disabled, serve requires tokio and either http1 or http2. The default #[tokio::main] runtime also needs the application's Tokio macros and rt-multi-thread features.

findings.title: Update historical route syntax before reuse
findings.guidance: Use /{id} and /{*rest} captures. Historical /:id and /*rest patterns panic under the normal 0.8 checks. Wildcards do not cover the bare prefix or its trailing slash; register those paths separately when needed. Automatic trailing-slash redirects are absent.

findings.title: Separate nested-router and method fallback behavior
findings.guidance: A router nested with nest inherits the outer fallback unless it supplies its own. nest_service does not inherit fallbacks. MethodRouter fallbacks handle unmatched methods, and merging two method routers that both have custom fallbacks panics. Set one fallback after merging.

findings.title: Use typed state and inexpensive clones
findings.guidance: Prefer State for application-wide data. Router<S> represents a router still missing S; supply it with with_state before serving. Keep state clones cheap, using Arc where appropriate. Implement FromRef for substates, or enable macros to derive it. A missing required Extension causes a runtime 500.

findings.title: Order extractors around one body consumer
findings.guidance: Extractors run left to right. Put Path, Query, headers, and State before the single body-consuming extractor. Json, Form, String, Bytes, and Request occupy the final position when used. JSON needs a suitable content type; Form reads GET/HEAD query strings and otherwise expects an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body.

findings.title: Customize rejections through their public interface
findings.guidance: Use Result<Json<T>, JsonRejection> for handler-local error customization, or wrap Json in a custom extractor for reuse. Public status() and body_text() methods support an error envelope without inspecting internal error types. Internal-source downcasts can break without a major release.

findings.title: Check each optional extractor's actual semantics
findings.guidance: Do not use Option<Extractor> as a general error-suppression mechanism. In this release, Option<Json<T>> returns None when Content-Type is absent but still rejects an unsuitable content type or invalid JSON. Option<Extension<T>> returns None for a missing extension.

findings.title: Choose the appropriate custom extractor trait
findings.guidance: Implement FromRequestParts<S> for metadata and FromRequest<S> for body-consuming extraction, using native async methods. Avoid implementing both directly on one concrete extractor; generic wrappers are the documented exception. Historical request-body-generic signatures should not be copied.

findings.title: Keep body buffering limits explicit
findings.guidance: Bytes-based extractors have a default 2 MB limit, also affecting String, Json, and Form. When collecting Body directly with to_bytes, supply the desired limit explicitly. Its error source can identify http_body_util::LengthLimitError.

findings.title: Convert service failures into responses
findings.guidance: Handler Result errors that implement IntoResponse become ordinary HTTP responses. Fallible Tower services and middleware require HandleError or HandleErrorLayer. Place HandleErrorLayer outside a Tower timeout; any request-parts extractors precede the error argument.

findings.title: Account for middleware scope and ordering
findings.guidance: Add routes before applying their layers. Repeated layer calls process incoming requests from the last layer backward; ServiceBuilder processes them in declaration order. URI rewriting must wrap the entire Router because Router::layer runs after routing.

findings.title: Keep request context and backpressure policies deliberate
findings.guidance: Pass per-request middleware data through request extensions and insert it before next.run. Request extensions are not automatically copied to the response. Route-level concurrency middleware does not establish a general backpressure policy; the documentation recommends load shedding or placing backpressure-sensitive middleware around the whole application.

findings.title: Make response and error types inferable
findings.guidance: Use tuples to compose status, headers, extensions, and a final body. Convert heterogeneous branches into Response with into_response(). For question-mark propagation, give Result a concrete error type; impl IntoResponse alone does not resolve error conversion or allow unrelated branch types.

findings.title: Diagnose handler bounds and extractor failures
findings.guidance: For Handler errors, check extractor order, response conversion, Send futures, and Sync requirements. Holding a non-Send value across await commonly breaks a handler. Enable macros for debug_handler diagnostics. Enable tracing and configure the axum::rejection=trace target to inspect built-in extractor rejections.

recipes.title: Start a typed JSON HTTP server
recipes.description: Serve a greeting and accept POST /users with a JSON username, returning an illustrative 201 JSON response. Runs until stopped.

recipes.title: Compose routes and fallbacks without historical API traps
recipes.description: Demonstrate 0.8 wildcard syntax, explicit slash routes, nested fallback inheritance, and a shared method fallback. Runs until stopped.

recipes.title: Share application state and extract a substate
recipes.description: Build routes that require AppState, provide that state before serving, and extract only an Arc-backed substate. No macros feature is needed for manual FromRef.

recipes.title: Combine typed path and query parameters
recipes.description: Deserialize a UUID path and page/per_page query parameters, then return typed JSON. UUID serialization support is enabled without requesting UUID generation.

recipes.title: Return a consistent JSON rejection envelope
recipes.description: Echo valid typed JSON and turn every JSON rejection into a JSON message while preserving its status. The body extractor remains last.

recipes.title: Implement metadata and body validation extractors
recipes.description: Require a User-Agent header and a nonempty body using separate extractor traits. Delegating to Bytes retains its standard rejection and body-limit behavior.

recipes.title: Pass request context from middleware to handlers
recipes.description: Demonstrate middleware inserting per-request identity for a handler. The fixed token is illustrative; unmatched paths retain the router's 404 behavior.

recipes.title: Handle fallible services and Tower timeouts
recipes.description: Serve a deliberately failing service as HTTP 500 and a deliberately pending handler as HTTP 408 after one second, with error conversion outside the timeout.

recipes.title: Compose responses and resolve return-type inference
recipes.description: Show tuple composition, response extensions, a low-level builder, heterogeneous response branches, and a concrete Result error type. POST /create only demonstrates header validation.

recipes.title: Read and return URL-encoded forms
recipes.description: Accept GET /form?value=hello or a POST form body value=hello with application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and return an encoded form response.

recipes.title: Collect a body with an explicit byte limit
recipes.description: A finite program illustrating successful bounded collection and recognition of a size-limit error. It needs no axum server features.

recipes.title: Rewrite a URI before routing
recipes.description: Internally rewrite /legacy to / before route selection, preserving the query string. The layer wraps the whole Router.

recipes.title: Compose tracing, extensions, and a method concurrency limit
recipes.description: Trace HTTP requests, insert an extension before the handler, and limit concurrent calls through the GET method route. This demonstrates layer composition, not a complete overload policy.
